page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.18xlarge is a storage-optimized instance belonging to the i7ie server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon 8559C processors operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance offers 36 physical cores and 72 dedicated vCPUs with 2 threads per core, backed by 320 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and 48 KB L1d cache. System memory totals 576.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, which provides an allocation of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of 45,000 GB of NVMe SSDs directly attached to the host. Network connectivity is managed through the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline bandwidth of 75 Gbps. The CPU includes vector and instruction extensions such as AVX-512, Intel AMX (tile and int8), AES-NI, and SHA-NI, but does not feature GPU acceleration.

Performance metrics indicate strong capabilities across memory throughput, parallel computation, and I/O tasks. Multi-core performance is notable, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 69,824.62 and a PassMark CPU score of 82,956.08. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a single-core score of 2,297.0 and a multi-core score of 20,730.0. Software compilation performance reached 52,569.0 in Geekbench Clang tests. Memory subsystem testing revealed a read bandwidth of 5,448.13 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 287.15 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Application benchmarks recorded a static web serving throughput of 109.44 GB/sec, PassMark database operations at 32,734.62, and Redis SET throughput at 91.92 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost efficiency perspective, bundling 45,000 GB of local NVMe storage with 576 GB of DDR5 RAM on a single host offers high resource density, lowering the effective per-gigabyte overhead compared to assembling network-attached block storage. Tradeoffs include the lack of dedicated GPU hardware, which limits its suitability for large-scale deep learning model training or heavy LLM inference compared to specialized accelerator instances, despite strong CPU-based AMX acceleration. Additionally, single-core stress-ng performance falls into the average range. The server is well suited for resource-demanding workloads such as high-throughput relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, big data processing pipelines, web serving at scale, and concurrent software build systems.
description: Amazon Web Services i7ie.18xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by 36 physical cores and 72 vCPUs from Intel Xeon 8559C processors running at 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 576.0 GB of DDR5 memory and 45,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, along with 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The hardware includes hardware accelerations such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512. Benchmarks highlight strong multi-core compute capability with a multi-core stress-ng score of 69,824.62, top-tier Geekbench scores, and high static web serving throughput of 109.44 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth reaches 5,448.13 GB/sec for small cached blocks, while Redis SET performance registers at 91.92 million operations per second. The combination of dense local SSD capacity and high memory allocation yields strong qualitative cost efficiency for I/O-heavy workloads, avoiding remote storage bottlenecks. It is best suited for enterprise databases, key-value stores, real-time analytics, and software compilation.
